items.title: France's Safran pumps €136mil into Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: French aerospace group Safran Landing Systems is investing €136 million (about RM640 million) to expand its manufacturing facility in Sendayan and open a new carbon brake maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) centre in Nilai, both in Negri Sembilan. The investments comprise €134 million for the expansion of its Sendayan facility and €2 million for the new MRO centre, which will serve about 100 airline operators across Asia Pacific. The Sendayan expansion adds 7,000 square metres of manufacturing space, including a new textile production line, carbonisation furnaces and advanced machining equipment.

items.title: Malaysia to deploy latest body scanners at RTS Link border checkpoint
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — Latest technology scanners will be deployed at the Immigration, Customs and Quarantine (ICQ) Complex in Bukit Chagar here once the Johor Bahru–Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link starts operations early next year. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the implementation of this technology marks a first for Malaysia and serves as part of efforts to enhance security at the nation’s entry points. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail (left) presenting a memento to his Singapore counterpart Sim Ann, who is the Second Minister for Home Affairs, at the Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Security Exercise (FTX 2026) closing ceremony at the RTS Link Wadi Hana site Johor Bahru today, Oct 28, 2026.

items.title: Headmaster given 20 years' jail, rotan for pornography, sexual assault of student, 12
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A headmaster was sentenced to 20 years' jail and 11 strokes of the rotan after the Court of Appeal found him guilty of producing child pornography and sexual assault of a 12-year-old student five years ago. The court also allowed the prosecution's appeal of the 59-year-old's acquittal on the sexual assault charge which had been delivered by a lower court. On the sexual assault charge, the appellate court sentenced Anuar to 10 years' jail and one stroke of the rotan, as well as an extra year and two strokes under Section 16(1) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.

items.title: MCA accepts two seats for Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MCA has accepted the two seats allocated to it by Barisan Nasional (BN) for the Melaka state election. Its president, Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong, said the decision was made after receiving assurances that the party's role in representing the Chinese community in Melaka would not be sidelined. He said discussions among BN component parties had yielded positive results, with BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi responding positively to issues raised by MCA.

items.title: Iran to woo M'sian tourists with historical and cultural attractions
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Iran and Malaysia are developing practical programmes in cultural and halal tourism, heritage protection and handicrafts. Iran's Deputy Minister of Cultural Heritage, Tourism and Handicrafts Ali Darabi, shared this in an exclusive interview with IRNA, according to TV BRICS. He also proposes holding an "Iran Week" in Malaysia to showcase Iran's cultural and civilisational heritage.

items.title: PN seeks contempt proceedings against RoS over registration revocation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional has applied to the High Court for permission to initiate committal proceedings against the Registrar of Societies (RoS) over the revocation of its registration. The application was filed by PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan and four other party leaders, naming Registrar of Societies Datuk Mohd Zulfikar Ahmad as the respondent. Lawyer Rafique Rashid Ali confirmed that the application was filed yesterday.

items.title: Ex-convicts among nine arrested in Miri grave desecration probe
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 28 — Police have arrested nine men believed to be involved in grave desecration activities in the Miri district during a special operation from October 11 to 17. Sarawak acting police commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said investigations revealed that three of the suspects had prior criminal records. "Following our action and investigations, police have solved 15 reported grave desecration cases in the Miri district.

items.title: E-Commerce Bill to include licensing rules – Armizan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The E-Commerce Bill, aimed at strengthening accountability among online platforms and sellers, is being revised to include a licensing regime. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Seri Armizan Mohd Ali said the ministry was ready to table the bill earlier, but the cabinet called for further improvements. Armizan said the bill would focus on four key areas.

items.title: Man remanded over Facebook caricature allegedly insulting police
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 28 — Police have arrested a 50-year-old local man in connection with an investigation into a caricature allegedly insulting the police that went viral on social media. In a statement today, Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said the 50-year-old self-employed man was detained outside Menara Seri Wilayah P2a in Putrajaya yesterday. Adzli said police had seized a mobile phone believed to have been used to make the post.

items.title: Perlis considers removing jetty wall after MMEA sailor killed
items.summary: ARAU: The Perlis government will consider removing the concrete wall of an old jetty in Sungai Padang after a Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) patrol boat struck it two days ago. The crash threw four sailors overboard, killing one. He added that the state government would finalise assistance for the widow and family of 41-year-old Leading Seaman (Technical) Mohd Roshaimi Mohd Ridzuan.

items.title: Zahid signals unity amid BN-MCA seat dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has sought to reassure the coalition's members amid a dispute with MCA over seat allocations for the Melaka election. In a Facebook post, Zahid shared an image of himself clasping hands with MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong, with BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir standing beside them. Yesterday, Zahid said seat talks with MCA had ended positively, leaving Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to announce the outcome.

items.title: States without sufficient water supply cannot host data centres, says Johari
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: States without sufficient water supply will not be allowed to host data centres, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani. Johari (BN-Titiwangsa) said the government said the government would consult state governments before approving data centre projects. Johari added that states should charge data centres higher water rates than ordinary users.

items.title: Motorcyclist riding against traffic killed in head-on crash with MPV
items.summary: MARAN: A motorcyclist was killed after riding against traffic and colliding head-on with a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) at Km 59 of Jalan Kuantan-Kuala Lumpur yesterday. Maran police chief Superintendent Wong Kim Wai said the accident involved a Honda Wave motorcycle and a Toyota Vellfire. "The Toyota driver was travelling from Kuantan towards Sri Jaya when a motorcyclist riding against the flow of traffic collided with his vehicle.

items.title: NRES to propose drought action plan to National Disaster Management Council - Arthur
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) will propose the development of a drought action plan to the National Disaster Management Council to strengthen preparedness for the phenomenon. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the proposal would be submitted for the council's consideration, so that action plans for floods and droughts could also be developed, in addition to the existing National Haze Action Plan. "This is something that will be brought to the National Disaster Management Council, so that, apart from an action plan for haze, we will also have action plans for floods and droughts," he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: What if a fire breaks out on the RTS Link? Malaysia and Singapore put their rescue plans to the test
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — Malaysia and Singapore have demonstrated their ability to jointly manage cross-border emergencies involving the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, following a field exercise simulating a fire aboard a stranded train. Singapore’s Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Second Minister for Home Affairs Sim Ann said the exercise, held yesterday, demonstrated effective coordination between agencies from both countries in responding swiftly and professionally to a simulated emergency. She said three key outcomes stood out during the exercise, namely real-time communication, coordinated deployment of emergency personnel, and effective command and control.

items.title: Boustead Plantations sale tests LTAT's priorities in protecting contributors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The proposed sale of a controlling stake in Boustead Plantations Bhd (BPlant) has put the Armed Forces Fund Board's (LTAT) choice of buyer under scrutiny, challenging it to secure the best value while safeguarding contributors' long-term interests. SD Guthrie Bhd, Tradewinds Plantation Bhd and Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd have been reported as contenders for the plantation business. Their proposals require LTAT to weigh sale proceeds alongside each buyer's financial capacity, operational experience and commitment to developing the estates.

items.title: Malaysians missing in Nepal: Perkeso review, cabinet hearing soon on aid for families
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH) says eligible families of the 54 Malaysians missing in Nepal will receive immediate Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) payouts. He said Perkeso needed the identity card numbers of the missing, which the families had not previously collected. Manivannan said Ramanan would also bring MASFIH's request for one-off humanitarian aid for all 54 families to the cabinet meeting this Friday.

items.title: MyCC proposes action against 18 enterprises over RM108.3mil bid rigging
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) has proposed action against 18 enterprises over bid-rigging in 30 public tenders worth RM108.3 million. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the tenders involved food supplies, including for schools and public universities, as well as cleaning services. He said the enterprises were allowed to make representations to MyCC.

items.title: 'You are a liar!' US-Cuba shouting match erupts at UN
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: A furious shouting match between representatives of the United States and Cuba prompted the temporary suspension of debate at the UN General Assembly on Tuesday. The debate this year, however, is taking place amid a major new pressure campaign by Washington against Cuba, including an oil blockade and broad sanctions that have severely crippled Cuba's economy. Rodriguez shouted back.

items.title: Ex-Selangau MP Baru Bian fails to throw out PKR’s RM10m lawsuit over party exit
items.summary: The court ordered the former Selangau Member of Parliament to pay RM4,000 in costs to PKR. Baru is among 16 former Members of Parliament and state assemblymen sued by PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh on behalf of the party for allegedly breaching the terms of a RM10 million bond they signed with the party. Also named as defendants are Datuk Kamarudin Jaffar, Datuk Mansor Othman, Datuk Mohd Rashid Hasnon, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah and Datuk Seri R. Santhara Kumar.

items.title: GPS to contest all 82 seats in Sarawak election, says Abang Johari
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 28 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) will contest all 82 state seats in Sarawak’s 13th state election. Sarawak Premier and GPS chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg said the decision was reached following a meeting with the presidents of the coalition’s component parties today. GPS comprises Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP.

items.title: 'Cruise for life' dream ends with 200 passengers stranded in Cambodia
items.summary: SIHANOUKVILLE: Around 200 passengers who paid to live on a cruise ship while travelling the world were abruptly left in a Cambodian port after the company ran out of money, an official said on Wednesday. US-based operator Villa Vie Residences announced on Tuesday it had "suspended operations in Cambodia" as it worked to address "extraordinary increases" in fuel costs following the Iran war. Villa Vie said it was "working with residents to coordinate disembarkation and identify temporary living arrangements."

items.title: Motorcyclist killed in Klang after collision with 4WD sends him into trailer’s path
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 28 — A motorcyclist was killed after being run over by a trailer following a collision with a four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicle travelling in the emergency lane along Jalan Pintasan Pelabuhan Barat, Klang, near here at 9am today. Klang Selatan police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the 37-year-old local man was pronounced dead at the scene due to severe injuries. The impact caused him to fall into the right lane, where he was run over by a trailer travelling in the adjacent lane.

items.title: All approved school projects will be completed, Fadhlina pledges
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The government has given its assurance that all approved school development projects will be implemented and completed, while projects that had to be cancelled due to specific factors will be resubmitted for fresh approval. Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said issues such as land constraints and rising costs would not result in school development needs being neglected, adding that affected projects would be resubmitted to address the needs of the schools concerned. She said 131 new school construction and replacement projects, costing more than RM14.789 billion in total, had been approved between 2023 and 2027.

items.title: Maxis shares slip after reports of revived merger plans with U Mobile
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Maxis Bhd shares slipped in late trading today following reports of renewed plans for a potential merger with U Mobile Sdn Bhd, which could create the country's largest wireless operator. At 4.30pm, Maxis shares fell 16 sen, or 4.38 per cent, to RM3.49, with 3.98 million shares traded. In 2024, Maxis had an early discussion on consideration of buying out U Mobile, reports said.

items.title: Four charged with trafficking maid who suffered severe burns
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH: Four people, including a married couple, were charged at the Sessions Court today with trafficking an Indonesian domestic worker for forced labour, allegedly leaving her with severe burns. The accused, Cheng Dee Wen and his wife, Lim Yeek Fern, both 33, Yeo Ann Sheng, 25, and R. Maneemekalai, 35, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to them before Judge Rohaida Ishak. They were jointly charged with trafficking Siti Rohaya for forced labour exploitation through the use of force, resulting in serious injuries to the victim.

items.title: Klang art studio loses nearly RM2,000 in pre-dawn break-in, three nabbed
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 28 — An art studio owner lost nearly RM2,000 after the studio in Bandar Bukit Tinggi, Klang was believed to have been broken into by three men on October 24. The South Klang district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said that in the incident around 4.20am, three suspects were believed to have prised open the grille door and wooden door of the premises before stealing the complainant’s belongings. “Acting on information, the police arrested three men aged between 22 and 30 years on October 27.

items.title: From control to autonomy: Rethinking how managers lead
items.summary: ORGANISATIONS understand the importance of employees who are innovative, proactive and adaptable, yet managers often retain tight control over decisions, procedures and how work is performed. How can organisations expect initiative when employees lack the authority to act on it? Managers may assign responsibilities while retaining the authority to approve the decisions needed to fulfil them.

items.title: Govt plans national drought response as El Niño threatens extreme heat in early 2027, Dewan Rakyat told
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) will propose the development of a drought action plan to the National Disaster Management Council to strengthen preparedness for the phenomenon. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the proposal would be submitted for the council’s consideration, so that action plans for floods and droughts could also be developed, in addition to the existing National Haze Action Plan. “This is something that will be brought to the National Disaster Management Council, so that, apart from an action plan for haze, we will also have action plans for floods and droughts,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Court of Appeal upholds Perak businessman’s acquittal on 122 cheating, forgery charges in RM6m case
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — The Court of Appeal today upheld the acquittal of a businessman on 122 counts of cheating and using forged documents involving medical equipment supply investments worth more than RM6 million in 2015. A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah, Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, and K. Muniandy dismissed the prosecution’s final appeal against the acquittal of N. Narendran, 46, by the Ipoh High Court in January 2022. On the contrary, the High Court correctly identified fatal fundamental flaws in the prosecution’s case, rendering the Sessions Court’s conviction unsafe to uphold,” he said.

items.title: The Selangor royal aide who wasn’t: Man nabbed over RM1.42m car and property scam
items.summary: Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the 40-year-old suspect was arrested in Johor Bahru at about 5 pm yesterday following continuous intelligence gathering into 26 police reports received nationwide since 2023. He said investigations also found that the self-employed suspect had no affiliation with or official appointment at any palace or the Selangor royal institution. “In Selangor alone, 15 police reports have been lodged, involving losses amounting to RM960,020.

items.title: Teenager sentenced to 120 hours of community service for iron rod assault
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 16-year-old boy with alleged links to a secret society was ordered to perform 120 hours of community service within six months after pleading guilty to assaulting two teenagers with an iron rod. The foundation said the boy regretted his actions and had no intention of repeating them. She directed that the community service and workshop requirements be completed separately.

items.title: HBA: The government intention to adopt a profit-based valuation methodology should be scrutinised
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Homeowners should not be expected to surrender properties they already own in exchange for promises of replacement homes under redevelopment schemes without adequate legal and financial safeguards. Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming has said the proposed legislation would complement existing laws governing dilapidated strata buildings, with developers' projected profits factored into determining the value of replacement properties for affected homeowners. Chang said.

items.title: Boeing narrows nine-month 2026 net loss to US$551mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Boeing's net loss narrowed to RM2.25 billion (US$551 million) in the first nine months of 2026 from RM24.38 billion (US$5.98 billion) a year earlier. Its revenue rose eight per cent to RM289.34 billion (US$70.96 billion) from RM267.10 billion (US$65.51 billion). For the third quarter, Boeing's net loss narrowed to US$116 million from US$5.339 billion a year earlier, while revenue increased four per cent to US$24.188 billion from US$23.27 billion.

items.title: Severe storm alert: MetMalaysia warns of heavy rain across KL, Selangor and eight states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning across several states and federal territories, forecasting heavy rain and strong winds until 8pm today. In Selangor, the affected districts comprise Hulu Langat, Gombak, Sepang, Petaling, and Hulu Selangor. Other peninsular locations on alert include Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, and Muallim), Pahang (Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Jerantut, and Raub), Negeri Sembilan (Seremban, Rembau, Port Dickson, and Jelebu), and Johor (Batu Pahat, Kluang, Kota Tinggi, Johor Bahru, Pontian, and Kulai).

items.title: Pahang exco tells ECRL passengers to beware of ticket scams
items.summary: KUANTAN: East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) passengers have been told to buy tickets only through authorised channels to avoid scams ahead of sales opening next month. Pahang Consumer Affairs and Human Resources Committee chairman Sim Chon Siang said scammers might exploit the anticipated demand by offering tickets at unusually low prices, including on social media. Some may offer discounted tickets to lure buyers, so passengers must remain vigilant.

items.title: Customs foils bid to transit RM49.5mil AI chips through Malaysia, with potential weapons applications [WATCH]
items.summary: SEPANG: The Customs Department has foiled an attempt to use Malaysia as a transit point to smuggle advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips worth RM49.5 million to another Asian country. The attempt was uncovered on Oct 15 when Customs officers seized 30 server units containing advanced AI chips at a warehouse in Kuala Lumpur International Airport's (KLIA) Free Commercial Zone. KLIA Customs director Aspalila AG Tuah said the servers had been brought into Malaysia from an undisclosed Asian country under a single air waybill and were intended for re-export to another Asian country.

items.title: Fewer foreign workers, more jobs for Malaysians: DPM Zahid outlines government’s priorities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The government will continue implementing measures to gradually reduce the country’s reliance on foreign workers, in line with the direction set out in the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. In a Facebook post today, Ahmad Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the efforts would take into account the actual needs of industries while prioritising employment opportunities for Malaysians. Ahmad Zahid said he had highlighted the matter while chairing the third Cabinet Committee Meeting on Foreign Workers at Parliament today.

items.title: GPS to contest all 82 seats in Sarawak polls – Abang Johari
items.summary: KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) will contest all 82 seats in the upcoming 13th Sarawak state election. Its chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg, who is also Sarawak Premier, said the decision was finalised at a GPS meeting attended by the presidents of all four component parties. He said the coalition was ready for the election, although the Election Commission (EC) had yet to announce the date.

items.title: Tun Faisal hits back at Tuan Ibrahim over call for Bersatu to quit PN
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Bersatu information chief Datuk Tun Faisal Ismail Aziz has slammed Pas deputy president Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man for calling on the party to leave Perikatan Nasional amid the coalition's internal crisis. Tun Faisal said the crisis stemmed from Pas leaders violating the PN constitution and treating their coalition partner unfairly. "What is wrong with Pas?

items.title: Ex-Esscom intel chief says he was held in dark room in RM190mil suit
items.summary: TAWAU: Former Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscomm) intelligence chief Senior Assistant Commissioner (R) Datuk Mat Zaki Md Zain claimed he was held in a dark room during detention over a murder investigation. Mat Zaki claimed the room, known as "Blok Insaf", was commonly used to house prisoners considered disruptive, violent or mentally unwell. Mat Zaki disagreed with the suggestion that prison management, cell control, block assignments and the security of prisoners or detainees at Tawau Prison fell entirely under the authority of the prison director and the Prisons Act 1995.

items.title: MACC monitoring over, but HRD Corp must now show results from RM2b training levies, says MEF
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has called on the Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) to prioritise skills development, training quality and measurable workplace outcomes following the conclusion of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) governance monitoring of the agency. MEF Senior Advisor for Government, Media and International Engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the conclusion of the monitoring marked an important step towards restoring employers’ confidence in HRD Corp following the implementation of governance improvement measures. “The conclusion of MACC’s governance monitoring is a positive development.

items.title: Govt may use international legal mechanisms to claim compensation for transboundary haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is open to considering suitable international legal mechanisms to seek compensation for transboundary haze. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the option could be explored as the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution currently has no provision for compensation claims between states. "However, the government is open to examining other legal mechanisms, subject to the basis of international law.

items.title: [UPDATED] Drug syndicates use luxury condos to evade police
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Drug syndicates are renting luxury condominiums with tight security to hide their operations and evade police. Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the properties were used to store drugs before they were moved elsewhere for distribution. He said the condominiums' strict security arrangements made it harder for police to gain access during raids.

items.title: [UPDATED]: Three drug syndicates busted, nearly 394kg of drugs worth RM2.15mil seized
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police have crippled three drug distribution syndicates operating in the Klang Valley, seizing nearly 394kg of drugs worth RM2.15 million in nine raids conducted over four days. City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the operations were carried out by the Kuala Lumpur and Cheras Narcotics Crime Investigation Departments. Fadil said the first operation, conducted between Oct 19 and 21, involved four raids at three condominiums in Sungai Besi, Cheras and Bandar Baru Seri Petaling.

items.title: Who’s behind the haze? No conclusive evidence linking Malaysian firms to Indonesia fires, says Arthur Kurup
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — There is no conclusive evidence that Malaysian-linked plantation companies were responsible for fires in Indonesia, Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said. He said NRES and the Plantation and Commodities Ministry had examined allegations that Malaysian companies were involved in burning activities in Indonesia. Arthur said the proposal to restrict financing for companies proven to be responsible for haze pollution required further scrutiny, particularly regarding the legal basis, evidentiary standards, jurisdiction and implications for the financial sector.

items.title: ‘All is well, kita Geng Biru’: Zahid signals unity after meeting MCA’s Wee Ka Siong amid Melaka seat row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir met MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong at the Parliament building today, believed to be over seat allocation ahead of the Melaka state election. The three leaders were seen entering the Members of Parliament Block at about 12.20pm amid a dispute over the announcement of BN candidates for the polls. MCA leaders are also understood to be scheduled to hold a meeting at Wisma MCA this afternoon following the meeting.

items.title: Botched Pahang raid leaves member of public injured, National Anti-Drugs Agency considers body cameras for officers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) will discuss with the Home Ministry (KDN) a proposal to seek funding from the Finance Ministry for the procurement of body cameras for its enforcement officers. Its director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the move followed a recommendation by the Enforcement Agency Integrity Commission (EAIC) for KDN to prioritise the provision of body cameras for AADK officers conducting field operations. Yesterday, the EAIC recommended that KDN prioritise the provision of body cameras for AADK enforcement personnel following an incident during an operation to locate a suspected individual in Bera last year.

items.title: Family apologises to Bella Astillah over Muar woman’s viral grab-and-kiss incident
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The family of a wedding guest who went viral for grabbing Bella Astillah by the back of her neck to kiss her on the cheek has publicly apologised to the singer-actress. The woman’s daughter-in-law phoned in to ERA radio station’s 3 Pagi ERA segment to tender the apology after previous attempts to reach Bella through Instagram direct messages went unanswered, Berita Harian reported. “Our whole family tried sending Bella direct messages on Instagram, but there was no response.

items.title: KLIA Customs seizes RM49.5m in AI chips with potential military uses, fifth case in RM100m syndicate probe
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 28 — The Customs Department at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) foiled an attempt to transit 30 servers containing advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips worth nearly RM49.5 million without the required authorisation. The chips could potentially be used in the development of military technology. KLIA Customs director Aspalila Ag.

items.title: Behind Chow Kit shopfronts, Immigration uncovers alleged illegal money transfer network, eight detained
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — An illegal money transfer syndicate using the ‘Hundi’ system and targeting Bangladeshi nationals in the Klang Valley was uncovered after the Immigration Department raided three premises in Chow Kit yesterday, where the activities were being conducted under the guise of retail and wholesale businesses. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the special operation, which began at 2.37pm, led to the arrest of eight Bangladeshi men aged between 24 and 42 following a month of intelligence gathering. “The syndicate is believed to have targeted Bangladeshi nationals in the Klang Valley by using e-wallet accounts and local bank accounts registered under the names of foreign agents to conduct financial transactions.

items.title: KLIA Customs seizes RM1m in cannabis and ketamine hidden in shoes, toys and tool shipments
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 28 — The Royal Malaysian Customs Department at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has foiled two attempts to smuggle cannabis flowers and ketamine weighing a total of 16.39kg and worth RM1.03 million. KLIA Customs director Aspalila Ag. Tuah said the first case involved the seizure of seven packages containing 7.28kg of cannabis flowers worth RM582,400 at the Pos Malaysia International Mail Centre at KLIA on October 12.

items.title: Malaysia to introduce new rules on AI use in court within next few weeks, says Chief Justice
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The judiciary will issue a new practice direction on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) by lawyers and court officers in legal proceedings within the next few weeks, says Chief Justice (CJ) Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh. He said the move came amid concerns over the reliability of AI-generated legal submissions, which could appear convincing despite containing inaccurate information. Wan Ahmad Farid stressed that while technology could help accelerate the administration of justice, it should never replace human judgment, particularly when courts are required to exercise judicial discretion.

items.title: Lebuhraya Sultan Iskandar fatal crash: Cabin crew member now gets murder charge after initial drink-driving counts
items.summary: Iman Nafiz Fong Sabirin, 26, nodded to indicate he understood the charge after it was read out before Magistrate MS Arunjothi. The charge, framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, carries the death penalty or between 30 and 40 years' imprisonment and at least 12 strokes of the cane upon conviction. That charge, framed under Section 44(1)(b) of the Road Transport Act 1987, carries 10 to 15 years' imprisonment and a fine ranging between RM50,000 and RM100,000.

items.title: RM1m to look the other way? Two enforcement officers among five nabbed in Johor MACC foreign worker graft probe
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — The Johor Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has remanded five individuals, including two federal enforcement agency officers, on suspicion of soliciting and receiving about RM1 million in bribes from a foreign worker agency. Johor MACC director Datuk Hazrul Shazreen Abd Yazid said a five-day remand order until November 1 was issued by Magistrate A. Dhilip Nair at the Johor Bahru Court Complex here today, after allowing an application by the commission. He said the other three individuals detained were foreign worker agents.

items.title: All 11 suspects in Kuala Perlis MMEA officer’s death investigated for murder
items.summary: KANGAR, Oct 28 — All 11 suspects detained following the death of a Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) officer during an operation on Monday are being investigated for murder, said Kedah and Perlis Maritime director First Admiral Maritime Romli Mustafa. He said the detainees, who are suspected of being undocumented migrants from Myanmar and Thailand, are being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code, as the case involves more than just immigration offences. Yesterday, Romli said the incident occurred at 11.37pm when five MMEA personnel were attempting to intercept a boat suspected of carrying undocumented migrants in Kuala Sungai Padang.

items.title: In Shah Alam, former GLC executive charged with using falsified documents to claim over RM15,000
items.summary: Mohd Nizam Ibrahim, 50, was accused of presenting fake company quotations and cash payment receipts as genuine to obtain the payments from an industry and technology research organisation. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) prosecuting officer Mohd Alimi Mustapha proposed bail of RM20,000 with one surety and requested that the accused report to the Selangor MACC office once a month. Judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud set bail at RM10,000 with one local surety, ordered him to report to the Selangor MACC office monthly from November and fixed December 7 for mention.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan gazettes dismissal of Sungei Ujong and Jelebu Undang following royal decree
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The dismissals of the former Undang of Sungei Ujong and Undang of Jelebu have been officially gazetted following a decree by Negeri Sembilan Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, formalising their removal amid an ongoing customary and political impasse. According to state gazettes dated October 23, Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin confirmed the removals complied with Article 16(1) of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959, The Star reported. The first gazette noted that a special session of the DKU was formally apprised of the decision by the Telaga Undang (the customary electoral body) of Luak Sungei Ujong to dismiss former undang Datuk Mubarak Dohak.

items.title: Terengganu MB pledges tighter oversight after 20 state firms record RM24m losses
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 28 — The Terengganu state government is conducting regular monitoring and improving management to restore the financial performance of its subsidiaries, after 20 of the 26 companies recorded combined losses of RM24.01 million in 2024. Terengganu Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the state government conducts internal audits and works with the National Audit Department to monitor the financial position, operational performance and challenges facing government-linked companies (GLCs). He said the state government held meetings almost every month to assess the companies’ progress, including reviewing financial reports and identifying necessary improvements.

items.title: Sabah’s federal development spending hits 71.78pc, with 291 projects completed, says Hajiji
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 28 — Sabah’s federal development expenditure performance has increased to 71.78 per cent as of Oct 26, up from 52.07 per cent on Aug 10 this year, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. Hajiji, when chairing the State Development Action Council (MTPNg) meeting at Menara Kinabalu here today, said a total of 291 development projects have been completed in Sabah this year including Sekolah Menengah Sains Sabah in Kota Kinabalu and Sekolah Kebangsaan Buit Hill in Penampang. In this regard, Hajiji called on all ministries, departments and implementing agencies to intensify efforts to ensure that the remaining development allocations were optimally utilised before the end of the 2026 financial year.
